page: Google Cloud Platform h4d-highmem-192-lssd is an x86_64 architecture instance belonging to the Compute Optimized family. The server provides 192 dedicated vCPUs paired with 1488 GB of system memory, delivering approximately 7.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. Discrete hardware accelerators are absent, with zero GPUs present on the host.

For high-speed I/O requirements, the instance bundles 4027 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage distributed across 10 drives. The dedicated CPU configuration guarantees consistent execution without hypervisor-level CPU sharing or burst throttles. Complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not provisioned with the instance.

In terms of infrastructure efficiency, uniting high core counts with a large memory capacity and bundled NVMe media reduces multi-host network overhead for heavy parallel tasks. The trade-off involves managing ephemeral local storage lifecycles and addressing workloads that do not require GPU acceleration.

The hardware configuration is appropriate for large-scale in-memory databases, distributed extract-transform-load (ETL) pipelines, high-concurrency data analytics, and memory-intensive computational simulations.
description: Google Cloud Platform h4d-highmem-192-lssd is a dedicated x86_64 server instance within the Compute Optimized family designed for demanding data-intensive workloads. It features 192 dedicated vCPUs and 1488 GB of memory, delivering approximately 7.75 GB of RAM per core without discrete GPU acceleration. The instance incorporates 4027 GB of local NVMe SSD storage distributed across 10 drives, providing fast local I/O for temporary data, caching, and swap operations. Public IPv4 connectivity is not included by default. The consolidation of extensive parallel compute capability, large RAM capacity, and integrated NVMe solid-state storage minimizes distributed cluster latency while maximizing resource density. This hardware profile is appropriate for in-memory databases, large-scale ETL pipelines, real-time data analytics, and computational modeling workloads that demand sustained processing throughput and high local storage performance.
